While it's a hilarious article, I really want to know what kind of coffee maker connects to the internet that allows you to write scripts for?

My work has these automated coffee machines, there is an LCD touchscreen and you can choose from a bunch of different options. I looked the model up online and they are around 10k USD. Anyways, they do have ethernet. With a device that is already that expensive from the hardware side of things, and already has a computer in it to drive the touchscreen, it is kind of a throwaway to add an ethernet adapter, and a management console with all sorts of bells and whistles, customization, administrative tasks. It's like any higher end printer or router-- it is bound to have some remote management capabilities. The extra software features would be cheap to implement, and then when some customer asks "can this coffee machine do XYZ?" they can say, "Sure it can do everything!" And it's possible the machine wasn't designed to be scripted for per se, but the guy figured out how to send the right payload to get it to queue up the job he wanted, through whatever crappy proprietary management interface the thing has.

It may have been included so that the manufacturer knows how much coffee is on hand and has been used so they can ship refills or have a technician come service the machine automatically. I'm sure they are selling the data regarding what kind of coffee you like to Starbucks, Dunkin Doughnuts, etc.
